item.research_question: How can a room temperature M2–M3 phase boundary be constructed in AgNbO3-based antiferroelectrics to simultaneously achieve high energy storage density and high efficiency?
item.processing_route: Conventional solid-state reaction: raw materials (Ag2O, Nb2O5, Ta2O5) ball milled for 24 h, calcined at 900 °C for 6 h in oxygen, pressed into pellets, cold isostatic pressed at 200 MPa, and sintered at 1070–1180 °C for 6 h in oxygen atmosphere; electrodes coated with silver paste and fired at 560 °C for 30 min
item.test_conditions: Dielectric measurements from −180 to 440 °C; P–E loops at 1 Hz; breakdown strength measured on samples ~0.15 mm thick; cycling reliability tested up to 10^6 cycles at 400 kV cm−1; temperature stability tested from 20–150 °C
key_findings: Achieved high energy storage density (Wrec) of 6.3 J cm−3 with efficiency (η) of 90% in ANT55 at room temperature.
Remnant polarization decreased monotonically with Ta content, reaching zero at x = 65 mol%, while hysteresis became nearly free for x > 50 mol%.
Breakdown strength (Eb) increased substantially to 470 kV cm−1 for ANT55 and 550 kV cm−1 for ANT65.
Energy storage density of ANT55 showed minimal variation (<5%) over a temperature range of 25–150 °C.
Cycling reliability was excellent, with energy storage density and efficiency maintaining values after 10^6 cycles.
Discharge energy density of 6.1 J cm−3 was achieved with a discharge time (t0.9) of less than 15 μs.
Synchrotron X-ray diffraction and STEM confirmed the existence of a room temperature M2–M3 phase boundary in the 50–60 mol% Ta range.
item.mechanism: The construction of a diffused M2–M3 phase boundary at room temperature stabilizes the antiferroelectric phase while introducing relaxor features through local structure heterogeneity. This heterogeneity smears the antiferroelectric-ferroelectric phase transition, reducing remnant polarization and hysteresis, which leads to high efficiency. The improved breakdown strength is attributed to reduced grain size, higher relative bulk density, wider band gap, and decreased polarization maxima.
item.limitations: The text notes that the breakdown strength is sample dimension dependent, and while bulk ceramics achieved 6.3 J cm−3, the energy storage density would be further improved in multilayer ceramics and film capacitors due to significantly increased breakdown strength.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the energy storage density would be further improved in ANTx multilayer ceramics and film capacitors. They also suggest the material opens applications in electrocaloric solid-state cooling devices and hysteresis-free actuators.
quotes: high Wrec of 6.3 J cm-3 with η of 90% can be simultaneously achieved by constructing a room temperature M2–M3 phase boundary

The existence of local structure heterogeneity in a fully stabilized AFE leads to relaxor AFEs and thus effectively impede the formation of macroscopic domain and smear the AFE–FE phase transition process.
